evidence_spans.text: Geneformer is a context-aware, attention-based deep learning model pretrained on large-scale transcriptomic data to enable predictions in network biology with limited data through transfer learning.

In silico deletion of GATA4 in fetal cardiomyocytes significantly impacts direct GATA4 targets more than indirect targets, while combined deletion of GATA4 and TBX5 has a greater than additive effect on cobound targets.

Geneformer identified 447 genes whose loss shifts cardiomyocytes toward hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and 478 genes whose loss shifts toward dilated cardiomyopathy; pathways enriched include Titin binding and sarcomere organization for HCM, muscle contraction and mitochondrial function for DCM.
During pretraining, Geneformer gained a fundamental understanding of network dynamics, encoding network hierarchy in the attention weights of the model in a completely self-supervised manner.
Geneformer significantly boosted the ability to predict bivalently marked genes compared to alternative methods (AUC 0.93 and 0.88).
CRISPR-mediated knockout of candidate TEAD4 in iPSC-derived cardiac microtissues caused a significant reduction in their ability to generate contractile stress
CRISPR-mediated knockout of both Geneformer-predicted targets GSN and PLN in the TTN+/− cells significantly improved the contractile stress of the TTN+/− cardiac microtissues
Geneformer significantly boosted the ability to predict central versus peripheral factors compared to alternative methods (AUC 0.81)

fine-tuned Geneformer to distinguish cardiomyocytes from non-failing hearts (n=9) or hearts affected by hypertrophic (n=11) or dilated (n=9) cardiomyopathy with an overall out-of-sample accuracy of 90%
Geneformer significantly boosted the ability to predict the regulatory range of transcription factors compared to alternative methods, whose predictions were near random.

AUC ± standard error by fivefold cross-validation Geneformer: 0.93 ± 0.07 (bivalent versus non-methylated); AUC ± standard error by fivefold cross-validation Geneformer: 0.88 ± 0.09 (bivalent versus Lys4-only-methylated)
in silico deletion of GATA4 or TBX5 alone had a significantly more deleterious effect on their known cobound targets compared to housekeeping genes.
AUC ± standard error by fivefold cross-validation Geneformer: 0.74 ± 0.08

limitations.statement: The absence of a rescue experiment (e.g., overexpression of a predicted target reversing the effect) is noted.
The selected source chunks do not report a rescue, reconstitution, reversal, or epistasis experiment; that rung of the causal evidence chain remains untested within this extraction scope.
Causal relationships are not fully established; only correlations and perturbation effects are reported.
It is not specified whether the fine-tuning hyperparameters were optimal for each task; the authors note that hyperparameter tuning would likely improve performance.
No negative results or failure cases are reported for fine-tuning tasks beyond the comparison to alternative methods.

methods.description: Geneformer is a context-aware, attention-based deep learning model with six layers of transformer encoder units, input size 2048, 256 embedding dimensions, four attention heads, feed-forward size 512, ReLU activation, dropout 0.02, trained with masked learning objective (15% masked), max learning rate 1e-3, linear warmup, Adam with weight decay fix, warmup steps 10000, weight decay 0.001, batch size 12, three epochs. Optimized with dynamic length-grouped padding (29.4x speedup) and Deepspeed distributed GPU training (12 V100 GPUs, ~3 days).
